category.name: Manage Joint Use and Third-Party Attachments

derivation: STANDARDS-DERIVED. Every field traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body per _Collab/SOURCE_AUTHORITY_PACK.md section E, which was obtained for this round because the pack carried nothing for this category. Nothing is generalised from a client programme or a product.
taxonomy_origin: TAXONOMY ORIGIN, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FACT FROM THE DERIVATION ABOVE. The derivation line describes where FIELD CONTENT comes from: every field value traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body and carries its citation. It does NOT describe where the taxonomy comes from. Which processes exist, how they are grouped and what they are called is a practitioner synthesis of delivered implementations, generalised until it is product- and client-neutral. Of the 102 process groups, 43 originate in programme material, 28 in domain research, 20 in a published source and 11 in folder and file names; the provenance layer grades every one and names what to read next. This model is DELIVERED PRACTICE SPECIFIED AGAINST STANDARDS, not a standard turned into a model - and saying so is not a weakness. A taxonomy proven in delivery and then held against the standards is a stronger claim than one derived from a standard and never built.
field_set: EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2 maintenance process profile, corroborated by ISO 9001:2015 cl. 4.4.1 a) to h).
gaps: This is the only category in the model that NEITHER public framework reaches. APQC PCF Utilities has no pole attachment process at any level and the GFMAM Asset Management Landscape has no subject for it. The Source Authority Pack accordingly held nothing until section E was written for this round, and every source in this category was obtained here.

EN 17007 has no process for third parties attaching to your structures. It is a maintenance standard and this is a commercial and regulatory programme conducted on shared plant. Fourteen of the thirty-five anchors are marked as the closest named process rather than a fit - SER.2 for an access licence, BUD.1 for a rate formula, BUD.4 for attachment rental. The stretch is stated on the citation rather than hidden behind a plausible code.

47 U.S.C. 224(c) is the structural fact that governs the whole category. A State that certifies displaces the FCC entirely, roughly half have, and this reference holds NO State rule. Every process therefore determines the governing regime before applying a number, and 11.1.5 is the determination that does it. What any particular State requires is judgment throughout.
47 U.S.C. 224(a)(1) does not reach municipally owned or cooperatively owned systems. For those owners neither the FCC timeline nor the FCC rate formulas apply, and the category still has to work.

The federal rule is procedural and unusually precise, which is unlike the rest of this reference: 47 CFR 1.1411 sets 10 business days to determine completeness, 45 days to survey, 14 to estimate, 30 to make ready in the communications space and 90 above it, with named multipliers for Mid-Sized and Large Orders. Those numbers are quoted from the current eCFR. They are not described, softened or averaged.
1.1411(j)(3) states that self-help is not available for pole replacements. That single sentence is why 11.5 exists as its own group rather than as a tail on make-ready.

NESC is paywalled. Rules 235C, 238 and 250B are cited by number and subject only, confirmed from the NRECA joint-use guide which cites the 2023 edition. No clearance dimension or loading figure from their bodies appears anywhere in this category. The 40 in communication worker safety zone is NRECA's figure and is cited as NRECA's.
11.3.2 structural loading is a determination that passes the DMN test on shape and is SPEC because the arithmetic is NESC Rule 250B, which is unread. Writing that table would invent the numbers.

No source states an audit cycle, a sample size, an unauthorised-attachment penalty, a back-billing period, a transfer completion period or a double-wood target. All six are contract or operator policy and all six are marked judgment where they appear.
Joint ownership ratios and net settlement are universal practice and no standard describes them. 11.1.2 and 11.6.3 are judgment on that basis.

The reference names no transfer notification product. A multi-party notification exchange is the industry norm and naming one would breach product neutrality, so 11.5.1 describes the exchange and not the system.

Category boundaries held deliberately: 12.1 registers the structure and 11.4.1 carries the joint use overlay on it; 2.0 designs the line and 11.2.6 obtains the right to occupy somebody else's structure so it can be built; 5.3 posts the retirement and 11.5.4 clears the field condition; 16.0 contracts companies to work for you and 11.1.1 licenses another party to attach to you - opposite directions.
This category applies to electric only in model.json. Gas has no analogue: there is no third-party attachment to a gas main.

merge_corrections.what: Reconciled against Grok's independent specification of the same category, filed unasked twenty minutes after this one shipped. Six of its citations were verified against primary text and adopted, and one of them exposed an ERROR here: 11.4.5 said a complete inspection's data displaces the presumptive attacher average, conflating 47 CFR 1.1409(d)(3) with (d)(4). (d)(3) takes a challenge with its methodology and permits a statistically sound survey where a complete inspection is impractical; (d)(4) is what makes the result the presumptive number. Also adopted: 1.1402(p) and (q), which DEFINE complex and simple make-ready; 1.1405, the operative mechanism behind 224(c) certification; 47 U.S.C. 224(g) with 47 CFR 1.1408(a) imputation, absent from 11.6 entirely; 18 CFR Part 101 Accounts 364 and 366 in place of a bare Part reference; and 1.1402(i), (j), (k), (n) for the conduit vocabulary. Grok's notation was NOT adopted on three counts - it made the governing-regime determination SPEC and the loading analysis DMN, and both are the wrong way round.
